status_detail: Operational colocation/cloud data center at 45 Krupp Drive in Williston; third-party project database reports 2 MW and $14M, while operator/directory sources confirm the facility, address, colocation services, redundant power and fiber.
notes: Primary operator page is sparse but confirms FirstLight data-center business; Cloud and Colocation/DataCenterMap identify 45 Krupp Dr. Server Country supplies capacity/investment, so capacity_mw should be treated as tracker-derived rather than official.

project_name: Tech Vault South Burlington Data Center
aliases: Tech Vault Vermont Data Center Facility
status_detail: Operational commercial data center/colocation facility in South Burlington; Tech Vault describes 39,000 sq ft of data center space, LEED Silver certification, carrier-neutral service, 24x7 operations, redundant power and 800 kW generator support.
notes: Schneider Electric article says the original 6,000 sq ft South Burlington facility opened September 15, 2010; current Tech Vault page reports 39,000 sq ft. Server Country reports 0.8 MW/$6M, not directly confirmed by the operator page.

status_detail: Listed as an operational managed colocation data center at 208 Flynn Ave., Suite 2E, Burlington, with backup power, cooling/humidity controls, fire suppression and fault-tolerant network infrastructure.
notes: Found via data-center directories rather than a current operator project page; include as low/medium confidence because the facility is repeatedly listed at the same Burlington address.

project_name: St. Albans Large-Scale Data Center Proposal
developer: Undisclosed developer; St. Albans municipal economic-development officials involved
status_detail: Former St. Albans town manager worked with an undisclosed developer in 2025 on possible 8-12 MW or 50 MW data-center concepts; the plans fell through because grid interconnection/substation work was estimated around $30 million.
notes: No final design capacity was confirmed; sources describe alternative 8-12 MW and 50 MW concepts. Marked rejected because the proposal failed/collapsed before active permitting or construction.

status_detail: VELCO built an EMP-protected standalone data center on its Rutland campus; reporting describes a 6,900-7,000 sq ft facility, construction starting in June 2017, migration during March-September 2019, and operation for business, telecom and Vermont transmission-grid computing needs.
